assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology from proglucagon processing and incretin action through to long-acting agonists for type 2 diabetes and obesity is a rare case in which basic endocrine physiology produced therapies with very large clinical and public-health reach. The discovery chain is clear and the impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and the incretin effect) and Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, therapeutic rationale) are the strongest basic-science contributors, and Knudsen led the design of liraglutide and semaglutide. Mojsov's early peptide work is a real credit question and Habener is not on the supplied list, so a three-person configuration leaves some allocation unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many large, independent outcome trials and in widespread clinical use. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Mojsov's contribution and the dispute over credit for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) form are not settled by the supplied text.
A prize split between physiology and drug design may need different recognition for the two parts.
I am relying on my own recollection of the literature and have not independently verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors has produced durable remissions in otherwise refractory B-cell malignancies. It is a conceptual and clinical step change in cancer immunotherapy, building on cellular immunology and gene transfer.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the translational CAR designs and early trials, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Eshhar's original chimeric receptor concept is not among the supplied names, which weakens the completeness of any configuration.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up. Long-term durability, solid-tumor failures and toxicity remain open, but the core finding is firmly established.
uncertainties: Origin of the chimeric receptor concept is missing from the credited names.
Overlap with checkpoint-blockade recognition and its own prior prize may shape how the committee frames it.
Long-term outcomes in solid tumors remain uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Microbial channelrhodopsins used as genetically targeted actuators let investigators control defined cells with millisecond precision. This changed how circuits are tested causally in neuroscience, a field close to my own, though I weigh it by the shared criteria and not by familiarity. Originality and breadth of adoption are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsin function, with Bamberg's role in the early biophysics. Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal control, and Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photoactivation is also relevant. Six credited names is far too many for three places, so the choice is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Used for more than a decade and independently validated in many labs and species. Clinical translation is only starting (vision restoration), so the claim rests on a research-tool impact.
uncertainties: Credit split among six contributors is the main unresolved point.
Whether a tool of this kind sits better under the prize's expectations about benefit to human health than a therapeutic.
Allocation between the molecular discovery and the neuronal demonstration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines made from the L1 capsid protein prevent persistent HPV infection and cervical precancer, with strong population-level effects. It is a clear case of basic virology becoming a cancer-prevention tool.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach, and Frazer contributed to VLP vaccine development in parallel. Others, including Zhou and groups at Georgetown and Rochester, also have claims that the supplied list does not carry. Zur Hausen's earlier HPV-cancer link was already recognized in 2008.
assessment.maturity: Well established, with registry data showing falling infection and lesion rates and reductions in invasive cancer in vaccinated cohorts.
uncertainties: Priority among parallel VLP efforts and associated patent disputes.
Whether the already recognized HPV-cancer discovery makes this a continuation of a recognized area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signaling and opened proteostasis as a field, with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The mechanism is original, clean and conceptually influential.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently dissected the pathway in yeast, including Ire1 and Hac1 splicing. This is a compact, fairly well-defined two-person configuration, though other contributors, such as Ron, are not supplied.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism established for decades and extended to metazoans. Therapeutic translation is still early, so the case is primarily a basic-science one.
uncertainties: Clinical impact is indirect so far.
Contributions of other investigators in mammalian UPR branches may need to be considered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing led to nusinersen and changed the natural history of spinal muscular atrophy, a severe motor neuron disease. It is a persuasive mechanism-to-therapy story that validated splice-modulating drugs.
assessment.attribution: Krainer's splicing-regulation work and Bennett's oligonucleotide chemistry and development are the decisive complementary contributions. Other contributors in the SMN2 and SMN1 gene field, notably those who identified the gene, are not supplied.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of follow-up. Clear benefit when treated early, and the principle is now replicated for other targets.
uncertainties: Gene discovery (SMN1) and antisense chemistry may be judged as separate achievements.
Competing gene-therapy and small-molecule approaches may affect how the committee frames priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib showed that inhibiting a defined oncogenic kinase can turn a fatal leukemia into a manageable disease, establishing the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy. The clinical effect is dramatic and the model has been repeated widely.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound program), Druker (clinical development and the rationale for BCR-ABL inhibition) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are a plausible trio. The earlier discovery of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion is a separate part of the story, and Rowley's contribution is not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Mature and long confirmed, with decades of survival data. Timeliness is a question because the paradigm is now well absorbed.
uncertainties: Earlier cytogenetic and oncogene discoveries may need to be recognized alongside, which complicates credit.
The central figures have already received major prizes, and a late Nobel could be seen as retrospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR and the mTOR pathway as a central integrator of nutrient and growth signals has shaped understanding of growth, metabolism, aging and cancer, and underlies clinically used inhibitors.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast and defined it as a nutrient-sensing kinase, and Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and its complexes. Schreiber's rapamycin-target chemistry is also a credit claim, and the contribution of Heitman and others is not supplied. The configuration is therefore uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Core biology is well replicated and clinical rapalogs are in use, but the pathway is complex and some physiological interpretations are still evolving.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Sabatini and Schreiber, and Sabatini's recent professional controversies, may influence the committee's view.
Therapeutic benefit of rapalogs is modest relative to the breadth of the biological finding.
